fit: isolated oral thymol and endurance, grip and coordination in accelerated-aging mice
assessment: Treated mouse treadmill distance roughly doubled from baseline and the control average stayed near baseline. Grip strength was near baseline after thymol versus a 36% decline in control. Coordination favored thymol. Single-compound exposure, survivor analyses and no length-of-stride measure. Earlier GSA abstract and mouse work overlap in source lineage.

fit: fresh ginger in warm water and menstrual pain with conflicting tables
assessment: Fresh ginger is preparation-adjacent. The 120-student quasi-experiment supplies conflicting baseline pain values and severity counts, and no reliable follow-up comparison between arms. A numerically matching 2015 report is not verified as independent.

fit: ginger tea and post-dose pain ratings in a 50-student quasi-experiment
assessment: Two-hour post-dose between-group pain intensity tests favored the intervention. The report states p = 0.002 for the first and p < 0.001 for the other three occasions. Nonrandom allocation, no matched drink, unverified fresh-root processing and menstrual pain limit transfer.

fit: ginger and tea beverage against aerobic exercise with conflicting comparator reports
assessment: Original Table 5 gives ginger VAS 7.20 to 5.60 and exercise 7.40 to 7.40, while the abstract reports a 0.900 exercise change. Department-defined groups and no reliable comparative test. No fresh or grated preparation or Parkinson endpoint.

fit: self-reported ginger use and unresolved linkage to survey pain regression
assessment: Table 4 lists ginger tea or chewing among surveyed practices. Conflicting counts and ambiguous Table 8 ingredient labels prevent attributing regressions to ginger. Cross-sectional menstrual-pain survey with no verified grating.
